transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-10-09
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 54m
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Evan Liu (Redwood SE); Lena Cho (Orion Head Eng), Marcus Reed (Orion SRE), Priya Anand (Orion Product), Ravi Kapoor (Orion Security)
Artifacts referenced: ORION-poc-deck.pdf (shared), traffic-sample.csv (drive link), redwood-pilot-pricing.xlsx (link)

[00:00] Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick intro — I'm Samira, AE at Redwood, with Diego and Evan on the SE side. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Lena: Good, thanks. Appreciate you squeezing us in, we've been looking forward to hashing out the workload details.
[00:12] Samira: Great. Today we want to align on success criteria, typical QPS/concurrency shapes, token distributions, and then agree an initial benchmark plan and timeline. Diego, do you want to kick off with how we normally model this?
[00:22] Diego: Sure. Quick note — transcription may mess names a bit, bear with it — but generally we ask for a week of traffic and then we do distribution histograms: request size (input tokens), response size (output tokens), concurrent in-flight requests, and arrival process. From that we extract peak QPS, 95th concurrency, and tail latencies for target models.
[00:40] Marcus: To give context, our current prod traffic for the payments chat assistant is spiky. Typical daytime sustained is ~180-220 QPS. Largest peaks during settlement windows hit about 600 QPS for short ~1–2 minute bursts.
[00:55] Priya: Average input length is short — like 20–40 tokens for quick status queries — but we do have longer flows for dispute summaries that can be 800–2,000 tokens input + 500–1,200 output. Those are <2% of requests but heavy.
[01:12] Diego: That's helpful. So we'll need to model a heavy-tailed token distribution: many short requests, small outputs, and a long-tail of long document summarization. For the POC we can either filter to the top 95% of requests or include a full tail run to validate fallback behavior.
[01:28] Evan: Also important — what are your latency SLOs? Is p95 the primary metric or user-observed median?
[01:34] Lena: p95 is what product cares about. Ideally <600ms for the chat flows that are short. For the long summaries we're OK with up to 2–3s, but cost needs to be reasonable.
[01:44] Samira: Thanks. From Redwood's side we usually propose two bench configs: hosted baseline with our optimized kernels and batching (single-region), and a dedicated config with reserved capacity if you want predictable throughput. The dedicated cluster can lower p95 for sustained loads.
[01:58] Marcus: For security, we need to know about data retention and KMS. Can you confirm SOC2 and SSO support now? Ravi?
[02:05] Ravi: Yeah, SOC2 is table stakes. We also need customer-managed KMS and SSO/SAML integration. Audit logs must be available for 12 months.
[02:14] Diego: Understood — we will share Redwood's security packet. We support SSO SAML and integrations with KMS for private deployments; audit logs are standard for Dedicated/Private. For hosted there's tiered retention, and we can scope an enterprise add-on for 12 months.
[02:28] Priya: Back to modeling — how do you simulate concurrency? Our current infra has about 40 concurrent workers handling the model requests, but those are multiplexed on top of our API layer.
[02:37] Diego: We model concurrency as number of inflight LLM requests. Given your sustained QPS 200 and average response time (say 300ms) concurrency roughly QPS * latency => 200 * 0.3 = 60 in-flight. But with batching we might see different effective concurrency at the runtime layer. For benchmarks we'll emulate arrival traces and keep the same inter-arrival distribution.
[02:58] Lena: For the POC success criteria: 1) p95 latency for short queries <600ms, 2) cost per 1M tokens under $X — we'll put a target in the doc, 3) no data retention beyond policy and SOC2+KMS, 4) ability to run on Dedicated if needed.
[03:17] Samira: That's clear. We'll capture that as success criteria and include a cost estimate in the pilot pricing. Diego, can you outline the benchmark plan and the metrics you'll provide?
[03:24] Diego: Plan: ingest one week anonymized traffic (Orion supplies). We'll run three passes: (A) Replay 24h sampled day to validate distribution shape and basic latency/cost; (B) Stress run to peak bursts (600 QPS) for 5–10 minutes to see saturation and tail; (C) Long-tail summary run for heavy documents to test memory/KV cache and token limits. Metrics delivered: p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput, GPU utilization, token/sec, cost estimate per 1M input+output tokens, and profiling traces. We'll also flag any model OOMs or retry/fallback events.
[04:03] Marcus: For the stress run, do you recommend autoscaling or fixed reservation? We prefer predictable latency under peak, so probably reserved.
[04:12] Evan: For predictable p95 under peak, reserved Dedicated capacity is recommended. With hosted you can burst but you might see some fallback if region constrained. For the POC we can test both: hosted baseline and a small Dedicated reservation to compare.
[04:26] Priya: Timeline — we want results in two weeks if possible. Is that realistic?
[04:31] Diego: Two weeks is tight but doable if you share the traffic export within 2 days. Bench runs themselves take 2–3 days including analysis. So target schedule: traffic export by 10/11, initial baseline run by 10/13, stress and long-tail by 10/15, analysis & report by 10/16.
[04:45] Lena: We can try to get the logs by 10/11. Security will need to approve the export; Ravi, can you own that?
[04:50] Ravi: Yep, I'll approve and sanitize. We'll remove PII and provide schema.
[04:54] Samira: Great. A couple of details: what model family are you planning to run in POC? Any requirement for instruction-following vs summarization?
[05:01] Priya: Two main use-cases: 1) short conversational guidance (low tokens), 2) dispute summarization and classification (longer). We're open to suggestions; performance matters.
[05:10] Diego: We'll propose two model variants for the POC: a smaller low-latency model for short chat (optimized quantized variant) and a larger model for high-quality summaries. We'll include recommendations about quantization and batching. Also we'll test prefix/KV caching for multi-turn to reduce cold-start costs.
[05:25] Marcus: What's the expected token distribution we should provision for? We gave high-level numbers earlier, can you specify buckets?
[05:30] Evan: Draft buckets: 75% requests input <= 50 tokens and output <= 60 tokens; 23% mid-range input 100–800 tokens with outputs 50–300; 2% long-tail input 800–2,000 tokens and outputs 300–1,200. We'll model the arrival process with spikes matching your settlement windows.
[05:49] Priya: That matches our telemetry. For cost modeling we need per-token cost and amortized latency — can you include that in the deliverable?
[05:56] Samira: Yes, the report will include per-token cost estimates for each model variant and configuration (hosted vs dedicated) plus a recommended operating point. We'll call out when Dedicated reduces cost per token due to utilization.
[06:07] Lena: Any special infra constraints? VPC or on-prem?
[06:11] Marcus: For the POC we can use hosted if logs are sanitized; long-term we'd likely want a Private VPC deployment for data residency.
[06:19] Diego: Noted. We'll run the POC on hosted but ensure the option to replicate the setup on Dedicated or Private with KMS is documented.
[06:26] Priya: On metrics, include GPU types used and whether model was quantized — we need reproducibility.
[06:31] Diego: Absolutely. We'll log GPU type (A10G vs H100), batch sizes, kernel selection notes, and quantization level.
[06:38] Ravi: Security: will you provide an NDA or is there a pilot contract with data terms?
[06:44] Samira: We'll send pilot terms and an addendum for data handling. I'll include the NDA and SOC2 report link.
[06:50] Evan: One more item — tokenization mismatches can skew cost. Please share language mix and any non-ASCII heavy inputs.
[06:58] Lena: Mainly English, a small percentage of Spanish, and some code snippets in logs. We'll flag that in the export.
[07:05] Diego: OK. For the benchmark run we will: 1) run a baseline pass to gather p50/p95/p99 and token distribution; 2) run peak burst to validate concurrency; 3) run the long-tail summarization at lower QPS to validate memory and cost. We'll capture traces and provide a spreadsheet with per-run metrics.
[07:21] Priya: Sounds good. Who's the owner on Redwood side for the runs?
[07:24] Samira: Diego will run the benchmarks and Evan will help with profiling and cost modeling. I'll own contracting and pricing.
[07:31] Marcus: After the POC, if results meet criteria, we expect to discuss Dedicated sizing and an SLA.
[07:36] Samira: Understood. We'll include a Dedicated sizing recommendation based on projected utilization in the report.
[07:42] (crosstalk)
[07:45] Diego: Quick clarification on the stress run: do you want sustained bursts at 600 QPS for 10 minutes, or shorter higher peaks?
[07:52] Lena: Let's do 600 QPS sustained for up to 10 minutes to mirror settlement windows. If you can also run a 1k QPS spike for 30s that would be helpful to see failover behavior.
[08:01] Diego: We'll include both.
[08:04] Samira: Recap of next steps — Samira will send pilot pricing + NDA and security packet by EOD 10/09; Diego will plan benchmark and start once Orion supplies sanitized logs; Orion to provide logs by 10/11; schedule infra deep dive for 10/15. Anything else?
[08:18] Priya: Please include the sample traffic spreadsheet template so we can map fields.
[08:22] Samira: Will do.
[08:24] Lena: Thanks. This was helpful.
[08:26] Samira: Thanks everyone. We'll circle back in the follow-up email with links and calendar invites.

[end of meeting]

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-attributions and filler words; some proper nouns may be slightly off in auto-transcription.

Bench plan summary (short):
- Baseline replay: sample day replay to capture p50/p95/p99, token histograms, cost estimate.
- Stress: 600 QPS sustained 10m + 1k QPS spike 30s to validate tail behavior.
- Long-tail: validate summary flows (800-2k input tokens) at lower qps for memory and KV cache checks.

Artifacts to deliver: benchmark spreadsheet (CSV), run-level traces (logs), configuration doc (model, quantization, GPU), recommendation for Dedicated sizing, pilot pricing sheet.
